newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Short circuit sparks Prague Metro fire - operator.
newsitem.headline: Short circuit sparks Prague Metro fire - operator.

text.p: Burning electrical cables in a tunnel forced closure of a central section of Prague's Metro underground railway on Monday, but no one was injured, the system's operator, DP Metro, said.
DP Metro Spokeswoman Zuzana Knoblochova said that about 30 passengers were treated for smoke inhalation in the incident, which happened between two stations on the Metro's east-west A line.

"At 9:45 (0745 GMT) operation on line A was limited. There was smoke in the tunnel between station Square of Peace (Namesti Miru) and station George of Podebrady (Jiriho z Podebrad)," Knoblochova said.
"The reason was the burning of (electrical) cables" due to a short circuit, she added later after DP staff had carried otu a preliminary investigation.
She said that, although no one was injured, those who had inhaled smoke were examined on the spot as a precaution.
Line A is the second oldest of the three lines on the electrically-driven Prague system, which has been functioning since the late 1970s.
Knoblochova said service should be fully restored by mid-afternoon.
